text: Ingenuity achieved the first powered controlled flight on another planet on April 19, 2021, hovering for 39.1 seconds at 3 meters altitude.
Originally planned for up to 5 experimental test flights, Ingenuity completed 72 flights across almost 3 years on Mars.
Ingenuity made its final flight, Flight 72, on January 18, 2024.
During its final landing on January 18, 2024, one or more rotor blades sustained damage, rendering the helicopter unable to fly.
NASA officially concluded the Ingenuity helicopter mission on January 25, 2024.
Because Mars' atmosphere is less than 1% as dense as Earth's, its twin rotors spun at over 2,400 RPM to generate lift.
